facts.text: The only major-college player of the 1990s to record 100 blocks and 100 assists: Oliver Miller, 1990-91 — 112 blk, 103 ast.
Only two major-college players of the 1990s scored 1000 points: Kevin Bradshaw (1990-91: 1,054 pts in 28 games); Glenn Robinson (1993-94: 1,030 pts in 34 games).
Only two major-college teams of the 1990s made 330 threes as a team: Arkansas (1994-95: 361 threes); Kentucky (1992-93: 340 threes).
The only major-college team of the 1990s to lose just once (20+ games): UNLV, 1990-91 — 34-1.
The only major-college team of the 1990s to lose every game (15+ games): Prairie View, 1991-92 — 0-28.
Only two major-college teams of the 1990s averaged 100 points a game (15+ games): Southern U. (2×, best 1990-91: 104.4 ppg, 19-9); Loyola Marymount (1990-91: 103.6 ppg, 16-15).
The only major-college player of the 1990s to average 12 rebounds a game as a freshman (15+ games): Adonal Foyle, 1994-95 — 12.4 rpg.
The only major-college player of the 1990s to average 10 assists a game (15+ games): Nelson Haggerty, 1994-95 — 10.1 apg.
Just three major-college players of the 1990s dished out 300 assists: Greg Anthony (1990-91: 310 assists); Sam Crawford (1992-93: 310 assists); Keith Jennings (1990-91: 301 assists).

Just four major-college players of the 1990s made 130 threes: Randy Rutherford (1994-95: 146 threes); Troy Hudson (1996-97: 134 threes); Curtis Staples (1997-98: 130 threes); Keith Veney (1996-97: 130 threes).
Just three major-college players of the 1990s made 100 threes as a freshman: Keith Veney (1992-93: 106 threes); Curtis Staples (1994-95: 103 threes); Ronnie McCollum (1997-98: 101 threes).
Only two major-college players of the 1990s averaged 4 steals a game (15+ games): Pointer Williams (1995-96: 4.4 spg); Shawn Griggs (1993-94: 4.0 spg).
Just four major-college teams of the 1990s won 35 games: Duke (1998-99: 37-2); Kansas (1997-98: 35-4); Kentucky (2×, best 1997-98: 35-4); Massachusetts (1995-96: 35-2).
Just four major-college teams of the 1990s lost 27 games: Grambling (1999-00: 1-30); Fla. Atlantic (1999-00: 2-28); Prairie View (1991-92: 0-28); Howard (1999-00: 1-27).
Most 25-point-per-game seasons (15+ games) in the 1990s: Alphonso Ford, 3 (1990-91, 1991-92, 1992-93).
Most 800-point seasons in the 1990s: Charles Jones, 2 (1996-97, 1997-98).
Most 3-steal-per-game seasons (15+ games) in the 1990s: Pepe Sanchez, 3 (1997-98, 1998-99, 1999-00).
Most 90-point-per-game seasons (15+ games) in the 1990s: Southern U., 6.
5 major-college players blocked 160 shots in the 1990s (6 seasons). The most extreme: Adonal Foyle, 1996-97 — 180 blocks.
Highest scoring average in a season in the 1990s: Kevin Bradshaw, U.S. International, 1990-91 — 37.6 ppg.
Most points in a season in the 1990s: Kevin Bradshaw, U.S. International, 1990-91 — 1,054.
Most 12-rebound-per-game seasons (15+ games) by one school's players in the 1990s: Southern, 4 (Jervaughn Scales, Leonard White, Dwayne Tanks).
Most 200-free-throw seasons by one school's players in the 1990s: Milwaukee, 3 (Shannon Smith, Chad Angeli).
Best field-goal percentage in a season (200+ attempts) in the 1990s: Jelani McCoy, UCLA, 1996-97 — 0.756%.
Best free-throw percentage in a season (100+ attempts) in the 1990s: Matt Hildebrand, Liberty, 1993-94 — 0.925%.
Highest assist average in a season in the 1990s: Nelson Haggerty, Baylor, 1994-95 — 10.1 apg.
Most 3-steal-per-game seasons (15+ games) by one school's players in the 1990s: Temple, 3 (Pepe Sanchez).
Highest steals average in a season in the 1990s: Pointer Williams, McNeese State, 1995-96 — 4.4 spg.
Most threes in a season in the 1990s: Randy Rutherford, Oklahoma State, 1994-95 — 146.
Highest team scoring average in a season in the 1990s: Southern U., 1990-91 — 104.4 ppg (19-9).
Most wins in a season in the 1990s: Duke, 1998-99 — 37-2.
Most losses in a season in the 1990s: Grambling, 1999-00 — 1-30.
Best team field-goal percentage in a season in the 1990s: Duke, 1991-92 — 0.536%.
Most team threes in a season in the 1990s: Arkansas, 1994-95 — 361.
Most free throws made in a season in the 1990s: Kevin Bradshaw, U.S. International, 1990-91 — 278.
Most points of the 1990s: Keith Van Horn, 2,542.
Most rebounds of the 1990s: Tim Duncan, 1,570.
Most free throws made in the 1990s: Eddie Benton, 739.
Most assists of the 1990s: Ed Cota, 1,030.
Most threes of the 1990s: Curtis Staples, 413.
Most blocks of the 1990s: Adonal Foyle, 492.
Most steals of the 1990s: Pepe Sanchez, 365.
5 major-college players averaged 30 points a game (15+ games) in the 1990s. The most extreme: Kevin Bradshaw, 1990-91 — 37.6 ppg.
15 major-college players averaged 20 points and 12 rebounds (15+ games) in the 1990s (18 seasons). The most extreme: Kurt Thomas, 1994-95 — 28.9 ppg, 14.6 rpg.
8 major-college players averaged 14 rebounds a game (15+ games) in the 1990s (10 seasons). The most extreme: Warren Kidd, 1992-93 — 14.8 rpg.
11 major-college players averaged 5 blocks a game (15+ games) in the 1990s (14 seasons). The most extreme: Adonal Foyle, 1996-97 — 6.4 bpg.

method: College basketball (men's): each line is one Stathead (Sports Reference college basketball) Season Finder query over the decade's ten seasons (a decade is the seasons starting in its years: the 1970s run 1970-71 to 1979-80), run in a signed-in subscriber session; result rows and stable ids are stored as provenance.

Sports Reference's season finders begin with 1947-48, so the 1940s page covers two seasons and earlier decades are not in the record. Rebounds, assists, steals, blocks and the three-pointer (1986-87) arrive at different times; rules on a stat a season lacks return nothing. Per-game figures are totals divided by games.
